one_liner: Rust-powered terminal git diff viewer with side-by-side, word-level highlighting that renders huge diffs instantly.
description: termdiff is an open-source CLI that replaces git's default pager with a side-by-side, syntax-highlighted diff view. It does word-level change highlighting, hunk navigation with single keystrokes, and stays fast on monorepo-scale diffs. It ships as a single static binary and drops into existing git aliases with zero config.
target_user: Terminal-first software engineers who review diffs many times a day

icp.who: Senior engineers and OSS maintainers who live in the terminal and review large diffs daily
icp.pain: Default git diff output is unreadable for large changes, and existing pagers choke or misalign on monorepo-scale diffs
current_alternatives: Plain git diff piped through less
icp.buying_trigger: Joining a monorepo team or picking up heavy code-review duties where diff readability becomes a daily tax

differentiators: Renders a 10,000-line diff in 38ms — an order of magnitude faster than existing fancy-diff pagers
True side-by-side view in the terminal with word-level highlighting, not just intra-line color
Single static binary with zero config: respects existing git aliases and core.pager settings
proof_points: 4,200 GitHub stars within the first year
Benchmark in README: renders a 10k-line diff in 38ms on an M1 MacBook Air
Listed on Terminal Trove and packaged in Homebrew core

voice.sample_phrase: Your diffs, side by side, in 38 milliseconds.

signals: Issues triaged within days; 30+ external contributors

gaps: No demo GIF on the website
No comparison page against delta and difftastic

confidence.notes: Strong evidence from repo, benchmarks, and package listings. Adoption numbers beyond stars are self-reported.
